# lemma.id: relying-site integration pointers for AI agents

lemma.id is a private proof layer for web platforms: site-private PPIDs, signed backend verification, and optional isHuman assurance when one account must map to one verified human.

## Start here

- Human-readable docs: https://lemma.id/docs
- Canonical integration guide (machine-oriented): https://lemma.id/docs/integration/ISHUMAN_AGENT_INTEGRATION.md
- Repo agent entrypoint (if working in the lemma-enterprise repo): AGENTS.md

## Browser SDK

- Proof verifier: https://lemma.id/sdk/proof-verifier.js
- Create: `new ProofVerifier({ siteId: 'app.example.com' })`
- Signup/server verify: `await verifier.verifyForBackend({ autoProvision: true })`
- Compatibility: `ishuman-verifier.js` and `IsHumanVerifier` remain supported aliases

## Backend verifiers (local-first)

- Node/Workers: https://lemma.id/sdk/proof-verifier.mjs
- Python: https://lemma.id/sdk/proof-verifier.py

## Live demo

- https://lemma.id/demo

## Hard rules

1. `siteId` = canonical hostname (`app.example.com`), not internal `site_...` IDs.
2. Fail closed when `human` is false.
3. For signup/account creation, verify a signed `presentation` on the server, never trust a bare client `ppid`.
4. No customer webhooks, no wallet secret on the developer's backend, no KYC field storage.

## Out of scope for relying-site integration

Agent Ops (lemma-cli, Lemma Firewall, runtime control plane) is operator-only.
